questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to to Paris guided by a great interest in the French tradition for philosophy and further with the ambition of thinking in and with a new language, as translation is a theme that fascinates me a lot. It was my second exchange at Sorbonne and I went back with the desire to continue what I already started.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't know if this additional comment says much, but I found it way better being on exchange at Sorbonne on the level of master than bachelor. There are many reasons for that, of course, and not only factors that can be controlled my the exchange-program, however I had the feeling that master-program was more well fitted for students coming for exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: As I already said, it was my second exchange, and I have to admit that during my first semester at Sorbonne, finding information and knowing what to do was a mess, but this time, returning after an year or two, Sorbonne really improved on that point and I went through the semester without any frustrations.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a general meeting for all exchange-students giving information about the semester to come. And then there was a group of contact persons willing to help with any problems and questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding accommodation in Paris is difficult. I was lucky to have a couple of friends living there already and they helped me. But there are many groups on social media and on the internet, and with a little luck, that should do.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I prefer living off campus to integrate with the city. The idea of going abroad is also for cultural exchange and putting yourself outside the ''protected'' area of the campus makes you discover a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Student housing is not for me, so therefore my middle rating. However, I have met many people during my exchange staying at Cité Universitaire and they are generally very happy about living there.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All information about registration was given at a general meeting upon arrival. The course catalogues and time tables were available beforehand, so I already had an idea of which course I wanted to choose. Then there was prepared a google sheet where I could list all my courses and then a contact person would confirm them. The good things is that you can follow the courses for some time before definitively signing up, so you can ''try'' them out before making your final choice, in case of any doubts.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were a group of contact persons to ask.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got to follow all the courses I wanted. Sorbonne is very flexible on that point, its rare that students don't get there first priority

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read all information carefully. It's obvious, but it can be a little stressful in the beginning so the eyes are feverishly looking for an answer and then sometimes you miss it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses is high. All professors are very competent and specialized in the themes and questions they are examining in the courses. However, the style of teaching is very one sided, which I personally like, but it might too limit the potential richness of a more open dialogue.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is one sided, a professors speaking, students listening, no exercises in class. It's very very classic and traditional compared to the University of Copenhagen focusing on group work and class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Systématicité et historicité de la philosophie : Kant, Schelling, Hegel
- Merleau-Ponty, Phénoménologie de la perception
- Du phénoménologique dans la Phénoménologie de l’Esprit de Hegel
- Personsein. L’être en personne selon Edith Stein
- Séminaire de philosophie morale : L’éthique de Kierkegaard
- Temporalités des oeuvres d’art

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For students of philosophy I'll recommend courses under the formation ''histoire de la philosophie'', as this is the ''place'' where you get to meet the French tradition of thinking and working with the text. All expectations of the French instituions will be confirmed.

questions.answer: In general, the cost of living in Paris is a little cheaper than in Copenhagen. And then many cultural activities are free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a long list of activities but I didn't participate in any so I don't really know, sorry.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any, so I cannot really recommend any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Walk around in Paris, it's beautiful on many levels. And visit the banlieue for a bit of contrast to the very picturesque center. Many interesting things are going on in the outskirts of the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have lived in Paris before, and I missed it a lot, so it felt like coming home. You're going on an exchange so in the end it's more like a visit, so you don't really have to adjust in a profound sense. Of course there are differences but the excitement of all the new makes you forget the frustrations a bit.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be brave to cross the language barrier and simply talk.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It will be challenging, but if you feel drawn by the French language and for philosophy, the French tradition of thinking, it is truly special becoming part of it yourself. And then also open yourself for what is going on outside of the university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to study in a foreign language and meet a different way of thinking and doing philosophy.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam forms are very different from the ones at UCPH and it takes some time to be familiar with a new methodology.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
